title: A/R Summary lists Emile's Towing before Émile's Towing
custom_preconds:
Preconditions

  • Sign in as an Admin user (the "Admin" role).
  • Have two customers with open invoices on today's date whose names differ only by an accent: customer A, named "Emile's Towing", without it, and customer B, named "Émile's Towing", with it.
  • Use a desktop browser window 1440 px wide.
  • Open A/R Summary (Reports, then "A/R Aging Summary" under ACCOUNTS RECEIVABLE in the left menu).
custom_steps: 1. Without clicking any column header, find customer A and customer B in the list.
custom_expected:
Expected Result

Step 1:

  • The two customers sit next to each other (with the accent folded to its base letter their names are the same).
  • Customer A (no accent) is directly above customer B (with the accent).
  • The tie is broken by the plain lower-cased names, where the unaccented letter comes first.

Exact quotes from the source (for reproducibility)

From: PRD "A/R and A/P Report Sorting, Export and Location Filter", Confluence 947650561, version 9 (23 Oct 2026, Chris Ward), read 26 Oct 2026 · Epic SV-11315, story SV-11531 (Story 1, Reports open in QuickBooks name order)

  • S1-R4: “Two names that compare equal are ordered by the plain lower-cased name, then by the customer or vendor itself, so the same two customers always come out in the same order on screen, in the PDF and in the CSV. For example, "Emile's Towing" comes before "Émile's Towing": the accent folds for the name order (S1-R3), so the two tie, and in the plain lower-cased name the unaccented letter comes first.”
  • S1-R3: “Accented letters sort with their base letter: "Émile's" sorts among the E names (é è ê ë sort as e, á à â ä ã å as a, ç as c, ñ as n, ö ó ò ô õ ø as o, ü ú ù û as u, í ì î ï as i, ý ÿ as y, ß as ss, æ as ae, œ as oe, in both cases).”

From: Tech plan "A/R and A/P Report Sorting, Export and Location Filter — Technical Implementation Plan" (2026-10-21, uploaded 22 Oct 2026), read 22 Oct 2026

  • Tech plan §3 D4: “Name order name COLLATE utf8mb4_0900_ai_ci, then LOWER(name) COLLATE utf8mb4_bin, then the entity id”
